verses.1: Therefore, you must reflect carefully, oh human being who judge! For in whom do you judge the other person? You are judging yourself as well. After all, those same things are what the judge is actually judging.
verses.2: We know, however, that the punishment of God is indeed directed against those who do such things.
verses.3: But this is a reason, oh man who judges those who do such things and do them, that you have revealed the judgment of God.
verses.4: You despise the wealth of its usefulness, as well as its reliability and patience. You ignore the fact that the usefulness of God leads you to righteousness.
verses.5: But through your hardness of heart and your deceitful nature, you store up anger within yourself on days of anger, and you reveal God’s justice.
verses.6: Who will repay each one according to their own work.
verses.7: Those who, with patience, seek to do good deeds, will receive honor and praise for their efforts. They will also enjoy eternal life.
verses.8: But those who are forced into such conditions and actually convinced of this injustice, they will feel anger and resentment.
verses.9: Sorrow and depression, upon every soul of those who suffer from this evil, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.10: Glory, honor, and peace are all things that come from doing good deeds. This applies first and foremost to Jews, but also to Greeks.
verses.11: For it is not a form of hypocrisy towards God.
verses.12: For those who act contrary to the law, they will also be punished accordingly. And those who violate the law will be judged according to the law itself.
verses.13: For it is not those who uphold the law that are just before God, but rather those who create laws deserve to be considered righteous.
verses.14: For when nations that do not have laws naturally create laws themselves, then these laws that they do not possess are still considered laws.
verses.15: In this way, the work of the written law is revealed in their hearts. They act together, with their senses, and they accuse or defend each other’s arguments.
verses.16: On the day when God will judge the secrets of men according to my gospel through Christ Jesus.
verses.17: But if you are a Jew, then you must also obey the law and not act in a way that would bring shame upon God.
verses.18: And you will understand the law and test its differences by referring to it from within the law itself.
verses.19: And you also believed that yourself was a guide for those who are blind, a light in the darkness.
verses.20: To teach children without delay, to be a teacher to those who are young, having the essence of knowledge and truth in their laws.
verses.21: So, does he teach you something else, instead of just what he already teaches? Does he say that you should not steal, but you still do it anyway?
verses.22: Are you lying to me by saying that you’re not lying? Are you trying to deceive me by claiming that you don’t see those ghosts?
verses.23: Who is it that, according to the law, you dishonor by breaking the law?
verses.24: For the name of the God is blasphemed against you in the nations, as it is written.
verses.25: After all, circumcision can be useful if you follow the law. But if you break the law, then your circumcision becomes a curse.
verses.26: If then the acrobystia retains the rights of the law, then will the acrobystia not be punished for its actions?
verses.27: And it also condemns those who, by means of writing and tattooing, violate the law.
verses.28: For it is not a true Jew who is in the visible world, nor is it a true circumcision that is in the visible world.
verses.29: But the Jewish man in the darkness… His heart was pierced by a wound, not through words, but from God himself.
